actual_scope: Exhaustive census of the c=1 stabilizer, deciding whether any element that moves the trivial-character (+1,+1) 216-space preserves the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand and acts non-scalarly on it.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for a formal caller or certificate binding. The assigned question is open question 1 of open PR #7022: whether any c=1 stabilizer element that moves the ++ 216-space preserves the 8-dimensional dihedral isotypic summand and acts non-scalarly. PR #7023 already proved that summand reducible under A_1; this package does not reopen that proof. It does not add a Lean binding and does not change kappa.
bottleneck_link: Scoped side result on the historical centre Gram. The selected conditional kappa remains 781451/250000000. A mover that acted non-scalarly on this summand would enlarge the signed-permutation action beyond the dihedral image; the census shows that no mover even preserves the summand.
stop_rule: Stop once every c=1 stabilizer element has been tested on the 8-dimensional summand and the quotient rank of each mover image has been checked. Do not compute a characteristic polynomial and do not rerun the degree-881 certificate.
evidence: verify.py enumerates the line-preserving signed permutations and all 3072 c=1 stabilizer elements. Marker PASS_C1_MOVER_8_SUMMAND. Of the 3072 elements, 768 preserve the ++ 216-space and 2304 move it. Every mover satisfies s(V) perpendicular to V and s(V) intersect E = {0}. The named mover is the permutation (0 3)(5 6) with positive output signs. The 768 preservers act on V by +I or -I, 384 each. Selected baseline returned PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. The assistant enumerated the stabilizer and wrote the verifier. This is not an independent human or proof-kernel review.

open_questions.question: For the named mover (0 3)(5 6), does g or t act by a scalar on the image of the 8-dimensional summand?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The census proves that this image misses the trivial-character (+1,+1) space. If g and t act by scalars there, the image is one of the other three joint sign spaces. That names the destination. It is not the basis-transport question of PR #7019, whose 8-dimensional space lies in a nontrivial sign character and meets this 216-space only at zero.
open_questions.first_step: Apply g and t to m(w_0), where m is the permutation (0 3)(5 6) and w_0 is the first summand basis vector, and test whether each image is a scalar multiple of m(w_0).
open_questions.blocked_by: No missing input. This package stops once the intersection with the (+1,+1) space is zero and does not apply g or t to the moved vectors.

open_questions.question: Does any element of the line-preserving signed-permutation group outside the c=1 stabilizer preserve this 8-dimensional summand and act non-scalarly?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The nonexistence statement is scoped to the order-3072 stabilizer of sector c=1. An element that moves the sector is outside that hypothesis.
open_questions.first_step: Apply one element of the line-preserving group whose port map moves sector 1 to the eight basis vectors of V. The order-344064 group is already enumerated by the completeness argument.
open_questions.blocked_by: The completeness argument already builds the order-344064 group, but this package does not apply elements outside A(c=1) to V.

overlap.limits: Closed PRs were searched through local READMEs, TASK metadata and the ledger. No code diffs. The phrases 8-dimensional dihedral, moves the 216, and isotypic summand match PR #7008, PR #7022 and PR #7023, which ask or narrow the question, and PR #7019, which identifies a different 8-dimensional space. No open PR reports the action of a mover on this summand.
